decisions.reason: The adjustable quarter-pallet display sits close to the core offer and shares existing production capacity, so its results likely meet aspirations and give no reason to search for alternatives.
The pegboard-back shelf display is a low-cost variant of the established display line, and the large firm's slack lets it carry the product even if demand is uncertain.
The standard quarter-pallet shelf display is a core format for retail promotions and likely performs at or above aspiration.
The eighth-pallet display fits common retail space formats and uses existing capabilities, so it probably satisfies performance expectations.
The wooden pallet departs from the firm's cardboard competence and may underperform, but there is not yet clear evidence of a shortfall, and slack allows the firm to keep it for now.
Demand for media-product displays may be shrinking, which raises the risk of a shortfall, but the low marginal cost on shared capacity favours keeping it for another year.
